o1.biggest_strength: It turns the data into one blunt verdict — agencies are the only place we lose to Semrush, and Lite usage limits are the real churn engine — then backs each move with an owner, a first step this month and a measurable result.
o1.biggest_mistake: The claim that winning back a quarter of agency trials lifts new paid customers from 16.7 to 19.9 per 100 trials treats recovered trials as 100% converting, overstating move 1's return roughly five-fold.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the inflated win-back arithmetic with a defensible agency conversion target, and put the Lite limits fix forward as the fastest payback with the revenue at stake.

o2.biggest_strength: Every figure is shown with its working and calibrated — survey margin of error, confidence levels on where it is sure and not — so the owner could defend any line of it in a board meeting.
o2.biggest_mistake: The five moves are ordered but never justified: no reason is given for why the agency report outranks the Lite limits fix the data shows is the fastest money, and a short 'to confirm' list hands homework back to an owner who said they were unavailable.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give each move a one-line reason for its rank, naming the Lite fix as the fastest payback, and fold the 'to confirm' items into stated assumptions.

reason: Both find the same three signals, but Output 2's numbers all check out and it shows its working and its confidence, while Output 1's headline agency upside is overstated about five-fold — the kind of error that would embarrass a data-led brand.
